report.source_text: Ultrasound-guided biopsy (Figure 3) showed diffuse proliferation of large, atypical cells with clear cytoplasm, irregular nuclei, vesicular chromatin, and prominent nucleoli (Figure 4). Immunohistochemistry analysis demonstrated positive staining for CD-20, a B-cell marker (Figure 5) and Ki-67 staining showed a proliferation index of 60-70% (Figure 6). Further immunohistochemistry analysis showed atypical cells that stained positive for CD-45, BCL-6, and CD-10 but were negative for Her-2-neu, ER, PR, MUM-1, CD-30, ALK, and C-MYC.

clinician.final_diagnosis: stage IV, diffuse large B-cell non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 55-year-old Hispanic woman presented with a palpable left breast mass. Initial mammogram and ultrasound revealed an oval mass with indistinct margins. An ultrasound-guided biopsy confirmed diffuse large B-cell non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma (DLBCL) based on morphology and immunohistochemistry (positive for CD-20, CD-45, BCL-6, CD-10, and high Ki-67 proliferation index). Staging FDG-PET/CT demonstrated widespread metastatic disease, including diffuse osseous involvement, left breast mass with ipsilateral axillary lymph node involvement, bilateral pulmonary nodules, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, liver involvement, and abdominal lymph node involvement, consistent with Stage IV disease. The patient received six cycles of R-CHOP chemotherapy and achieved remission, which was sustained at a two-year follow-up.

Staging FDG-PET/CT showed diffuse osseous involvement, a two-centimeter mass of the left breast with ipsilateral axillary lymph node involvement, bilateral pulmonary spiculated nodules with ground-glass opacities, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, liver involvement, and abdominal lymph node involvement, consistent with diffuse metastatic disease (Stage IV).
